about: Popular newsletters with their homepage and, where it can be justified, their official feed URL. Edit freely. An entry is verified: true only when a live `npm run verify:catalog` run (the "Catalog check" GitHub Actions workflow) showed its feed or public archive working, and verifiedAt (UTC date) and verifiedRunId record that run; everything else is verified: false. Discovery validates every feed live before storing it, so a wrong entry fails safely. feedUrl null means: discover from the homepage. archiveUrl (optional): the public archive page to read when no feed is found. pickerNote (optional): a short line the picker shows with the preview. unavailable (optional): Impartly cannot read this newsletter (refuses_automated_access: the site refuses automated readers; not_on_web: no public source of its own issues that Impartly can read), so the picker explains instead of fetching, with pickerNote if set. note: for maintainers.

entries.name: TechCrunch
entries.note: Site-wide article feed (WordPress /feed/ convention); feed title TechCrunch, items are TechCrunch articles. TechCrunch's email newsletters do not have feeds of their own that we know of.

entries.name: StrictlyVC
entries.note: beehiiv publication (source given by Thalia, run 16). Live checks (runs 45337117393 and 45337784590) found no feed; /archive is read through the beehiiv sitemap (/sitemap.xml, 100 /p/ issues), newest "Wall Street's AI Rout Erases More Than $4 Trillion in Market Value" (lastmod 2026-11-21). Run 16's sample issue read only 458 characters (partial): the reader picked one paragraph wrapper. Fixed in run 17; Catalog check run 45342733284 read the newest issue at 11,744 characters, not partial. The old strictlyvc.com/feed/ (issues titled 2019) is not used.

entries.name: Morning Brew
entries.pickerNote: Impartly can't read Morning Brew's daily email from its website yet; forwarding is coming later.
entries.note: Live check run 45337784590: the homepage links the latest issue at /issues/<slug> and /issues/latest, but /issues/latest gave only 33 characters of text, no issue list was found, and the sitemaps list only /issues/latest under /issues/. /feed.xml and the news sitemap carry /stories/ articles, not the daily email, so they are kept out.

entries.name: Benedict Evans
entries.pickerNote: These are Benedict Evans' essays, not the weekly newsletter, which is sent by email only.
entries.note: No feed (the live check got http_404 on the feed paths). archiveUrl is his essays page, read as a public archive: the live check listed 10 essays by <article> markup and read the newest (not partial). It holds the essays, not the weekly email newsletter, which has no public source we know of.

entries.name: The Generalist
entries.note: Feed found by discovery at /feed (Substack-style); the live check showed feed title "The Generalist", site link generalist.com and newsletter posts (/p/...), so it is the newsletter's own feed.

entries.name: Axios Pro Rata
entries.note: Kept so a search for it explains itself. Live checks (runs 45279821252, 45327358059 and 45333404039) got HTTP 403 on this page and no feed or archive, which Impartly does not work around.

entries.name: Term Sheet
entries.pickerNote: Fortune marks Term Sheet as for subscribers, so Impartly reads only the public opening of each issue.
entries.note: Unverified. archiveUrl is Fortune's Term Sheet topic page (source from Thalia, 2026-11-24), which lists Term Sheet items, each on its own Fortune article page. archiveOnly: the feed Fortune advertises on its pages is general Fortune articles (feed title "Fortune FORTUNE" in the live check), not Term Sheet, so discovery never tries feeds for this entry. Fortune may meter or paywall articles; anything behind that is not read and the issue is marked partial. Catalog check run 45427728391 (2026-11-24): robots.txt allows the page; it advertises no feed; it lists 15 issues by JSON-LD (undated, newest 2026/11/24 "Tech gets Jensen Huang back, but not with a clean slate", then the 11/23 recap and 11/20 "Anthropic is now AI's bellwether"); the newest issue page is NewsArticle with isAccessibleForFree false and its body in the gated .paywall block, so only 181 characters of public text are read, partial. Not verified: no full issue text.
